correctness.rationale: The exact reduced-cardinal identity follows by cancellation of leading polynomial coefficients and interpolation uniqueness. The sum-of-absolute-values triangle inequality proves a uniform O(log N) norm comparison. Concavity of sin on [0,pi] bounds full-grid cards; angular localization and a compact boundary rescaling prove all three limiting regimes. The fixed-edge overshoot is strict; its inverse-square correction follows from globally localizing the exact sinc-ratio maximum. The packaged pure-Python checker passes 1242 supplementary finite assertions.

value.rationale: The sharp loss-of-sample growth answers a motivated stability question about an otherwise near-optimal logarithmic interpolation grid. The nontrivial boundary-layer coefficients resolve all three natural location scales, quantify fixed-offset overshoot and its inverse-square transition, and distinguish loss of edge from loss of interior observations. It is not a routine finite-table value or a renaming of a full-grid bound.
